text:
jamie (eng-runtime): Quick sync — proposing a new synthetic traffic generator to stress kernel selection, batching heuristics, and KV cache behavior. Goal: apples-to-apples perf comparisons across kernel variants and quant modes.

kai (eng-platform): 👍 want it to cover: steady-state QPS, short high-frequency spikes, and very low-rate long-lived tails. also replay mode for recorded sessions.

maria (eng-ml): We should capture KV cache hit curves explicitly. e.g., inject prefixes to simulate warm vs cold keys and measure KV miss cascades.

anita (eng-sre): Important: make warmup deterministic so CI repros regressions. random seeds + fixed start prefixes. Also measure p50/p95/p99.

jamie (eng-runtime): Agreed. Draft config sketch:
```yaml
phases:
  - name: slow-burn
    qps: 5
    duration_s: 120
  - name: spike-pulse
    qps: 250
    duration_s: 8
    repeat: 12
  - name: simmer
    qps: 40
    duration_s: 600
kv_cache:
  prefixes_to_warm: 1500
  pattern: zipfian
  ttl_s: 900
batching:
  max_wait_ms: 6
  target_batch_size: dynamic
  dynamic_alpha: 0.6
```

kai (eng-platform): I like the repeatable pulse pattern. Also suggest an oscillation mode (sine-wave QPS) to stress kernel selection switching frequency. Some kernels thrash on alternating sequence lengths.

maria (eng-ml): Add a per-request "prompt_length" distribution; short/medium/long to trigger different kernels. Something like 60% short(32), 30% med(256), 10% long(2048).

jamie (eng-runtime): Good call. Need to log KV metrics: hit_rate over time, cold-miss latency penalty, and how KV cache warming affects batch formation.

anita (eng-sre): For apples-to-apples: run baseline kernel (kernel_v1, float16) -> kernel_v2 (int8) -> kernel_v2 quant+fused. Keep same hw, same seed, same synthetic traffic file. Also snapshot system load (GPU temp, SM util, PCIe IO) concurrently.

perfbot: CI alert — benchmark run 1758000000 shows kernel_v2 p95 = 48ms (+9% vs baseline). Link: https://perf.internal/runs/1758000000

maria (eng-ml): When we saw regressions earlier the root cause was KV churn causing smaller batches. Suggest instrument: per-batch origin tags (kv_warmed vs kv_miss) and batch size histograms.

jamie (eng-runtime): Plan for instrumentation:
- per-request: prompt_len, kv_hit(bool), db_key_hash(modN)
- per-batch: batch_size, dominant_prompt_len, kv_miss_fraction
- per-run: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, kernel_selector_decision_count

kai (eng-platform): Also add a "no-cache" control run to quantify the benefit of KV caching. And a synthetic "cache-decay" mode to simulate TTL expiries mid-run.

anita (eng-sre): For spike measurement, record microsecond-resolution timestamps and derive inter-token time distributions. Microbursts can be 2-5ms wide and kill throughput if batching windows are mis-configured.

jamie (eng-runtime): Example invocation for a replay harness:
```bash
./synth-gen --seed 42 --profile=surge-chorus.yaml --replay=/recordings/session-2025-10-12.log --out=run-1758.json
./bench-run --kernel=kernel_v2 --quant=int8 --config=run-1758.json --metrics=prometheus_push
```

kai (eng-platform): Can we add an "alignment" knob to intentionally align burst start times across many clients to simulate correlated fan-in? Real traffic sometimes synchronizes on external triggers.

maria (eng-ml): Yes, and a jitter parameter to randomize alignment. Also include session stickiness so KV keys from same session have higher locality.

anita (eng-sre): For CI, gate on regression thresholds (p95 +5% or tokens/sec -6%). Keep wall-clock budget small by running shorter but hotter phases that expose perf cliffs.

jamie (eng-runtime): UX/outputs: single-line perf summary + inline histogram, and raw CSV of per-request records for offline analysis. Example summary: "kernel_v2 int8 | p50 12ms | p95 48ms | p99 220ms | tokens/s 18k | kv_hit 82%"

perfbot: New baseline comparison uploaded: https://perf.internal/compare/1758001234 (attached artifacts).

maria (eng-ml): Next steps: implement generator modes (replay, parametric sequences, oscillation), extend telemetry schema, and run head-to-head on our staging GPU cluster. I'll own telemetry extensions.

kai (eng-platform): I'll add alignment and jitter knobs and the per-batch tagging.

anita (eng-sre): I'll draft CI job definitions and regression thresholds.

jamie (eng-runtime): Great — I'll prototype the harness and add a small demo config. We should avoid coupling config names to kernel versions to keep comparisons clean.

kai (eng-platform): One more thought — include a "slowdown-injection" mode (add artificial per-request CPU jitter) to emulate noisy co-tenants affecting batching latency.

jamie (eng-runtime): Nice. Ok team, action items captured. We'll iterate on configs and run a first round by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:

anita (eng-sre): :white_check_mark:

maria (eng-ml): :rocket:

perfbot: Scheduled benchmark job 1758001234-1 queued on staging-gpu-pool.
